subject: Fundamental of Electrical and Electronics Engineering

questions.text: State Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL) and Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL). Using Mesh Current Analysis, determine the branch currents $I_1, I_2, I_3$ in a given three-mesh DC bridge circuit.
Explain Nodal Analysis. In a circuit with two non-reference nodes and a dependent voltage source, write node equations and solve for node voltages $V_1$ and $V_2$.
State Thevenin's Theorem. Find the Thevenin equivalent circuit ($V_{th}, R_{th}$) looking into terminals $A-B$ and find power dissipated in load resistor $R_L = 15\;\Omega$.
Find the Norton equivalent circuit ($I_N, R_N$) for a given DC network across load terminals $A-B$.

State and prove Maximum Power Transfer Theorem for DC resistive networks. Derive load condition $R_L = R_{th}$, maximum power formula $P_{\max} = \frac{V_{th}^2}{4 R_{th}}$, and transmission efficiency $\eta = 50\%$.

State Superposition Theorem. Calculate current through a $10\;\Omega$ resistor in a network containing two independent voltage sources of $20\text{ V}$ and $50\text{ V}$ and an independent current source of $2\text{ A}$.
Derive Star-to-Delta ($\text{Y}-\Delta$) and Delta-to-Star conversion formulas. Convert a balanced delta network of three $30\;\Omega$ resistors into an equivalent star network.

Explain Source Transformation technique (practical voltage source with series resistance $\leftrightarrow$ practical current source with parallel resistance). Simplify a given circuit using source transformations.

Define AC terms: Instantaneous value, Peak value, Average value, RMS value, Form Factor, and Crest/Peak Factor. Derive Average and RMS values for a pure sinusoidal voltage $v(t) = V_m \sin(\omega t)$.

A series RLC circuit with $R = 10\;\Omega, L = 0.1\text{ H}, C = 100\;\mu\text{F}$ is connected to a $230\text{ V}, 50\text{ Hz}$ AC supply. Calculate: (a) Inductive and capacitive reactances ($X_L, X_C$), (b) Total impedance $Z$, (c) Current and power factor, (d) Active power ($P$), reactive power ($Q$), and apparent power ($S$). Draw phasor diagram.

Explain Series Resonance in RLC circuits. Derive resonant frequency $f_r = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}$, Bandwidth $BW$, and Quality Factor $Q = \frac{\omega_0 L}{R}$. Explain why series resonance is called voltage resonance.

Explain Parallel Resonance in a two-branch parallel circuit (coil branch in parallel with capacitor). Derive resonant frequency $f_r = \frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{1}{LC} - \frac{R^2}{L^2}}$ and dynamic impedance $Z_d = \frac{L}{C R}$.

Explain 3-Phase AC Systems: Advantages of 3-phase over 1-phase system. In a balanced Star ($\text{Y}$) connected system, prove that $V_L = \sqrt{3} V_{ph}$ and $I_L = I_{ph}$. In balanced Delta ($\Delta$), prove that $V_L = V_{ph}$ and $I_L = \sqrt{3} I_{ph}$.

A balanced 3-phase star-connected load with impedance $Z_{ph} = (8 + j6)\;\Omega$ per phase is connected across a $400\text{ V}, 50\text{ Hz}$ 3-phase supply. Calculate: (a) Phase and line currents, (b) Power factor, (c) Total active power and total reactive power.

Explain Two-Wattmeter Method for 3-phase power measurement. Derive expressions for total power $P = W_1 + W_2$ and power factor $\cos\phi = \cos\left[\tan^{-1}\left(\sqrt{3}\frac{W_1 - W_2}{W_1 + W_2}\right)\right]$. Calculate readings of two wattmeters when load is $10\text{ kW}$ at $0.8$ power factor lagging.
In a two-wattmeter method, one wattmeter reads $5\text{ kW}$ and the second wattmeter reads $-1.5\text{ kW}$ (reversed reading). Find the total power and power factor of the 3-phase load.

Explain Magnetic Circuits: Magnetomotive Force (MMF), Magnetic Flux ($\Phi$), Reluctance ($\mathcal{R} = \frac{l}{\mu A}$), Permeance, Magnetic Field Intensity ($H$). Compare Magnetic vs Electric circuits in tabular form.

A cast steel ring of mean diameter $20\text{ cm}$ has a cross-sectional area of $4\text{ cm}^2$ and an air gap of $1\text{ mm}$. A coil of 500 turns is wound on the ring. Calculate the current required to produce a flux of $0.5\text{ mWb}$ in the air gap taking relative permeability of steel $\mu_r = 800$.

Explain Single-Phase Transformers: Principle of operation, EMF Equation $E = 4.44 f N \Phi_m$, Voltage Transformation Ratio ($k = N_2/N_1$), and phasor diagram for an ideal transformer on inductive load.

Explain Open-Circuit (OC) and Short-Circuit (SC) tests on a single-phase transformer. How are core loss $P_c$, full-load copper loss $P_{cu}$, efficiency $\eta$, and equivalent circuit parameters determined from test data?

A $10\text{ kVA}, 2200/220\text{ V}, 50\text{ Hz}$ single-phase transformer has core loss of $150\text{ W}$ and full-load copper loss of $250\text{ W}$. Calculate its efficiency at: (a) Full load at $0.8$ p.f. lagging, (b) Half load at unity power factor, (c) Condition for maximum efficiency.

Explain DC Machines: DC Generator and DC Motor. Explain Back EMF ($E_b = V - I_a R_a$), Torque equation $T = \frac{1}{2\pi} \frac{\Phi Z P I_a}{A}$, and torque-speed characteristics of DC Shunt, Series, and Compound motors.

A $220\text{ V}$ DC shunt motor runs at $1000\text{ rpm}$ taking an armature current of $40\text{ A}$. If armature resistance is $0.25\;\Omega$, calculate the speed if the torque is doubled and field flux is reduced by $10\%$.

Explain 3-Phase Induction Motors: Working principle, Rotating Magnetic Field (RMF) concept, Synchronous speed $N_s = \frac{120 f}{P}$, Rotor frequency $f_r = s f$, and Torque-Slip characteristics curve.

Explain PN Junction Diode: Forward and Reverse bias V-I characteristics, Shockley diode equation $I = I_s(e^{V/\eta V_T} - 1)$, Barrier Potential, Dynamic Resistance, and Zener Breakdown vs Avalanche Breakdown.

Explain Diode Rectifiers: Half-Wave Rectifier, Full-Wave Center-Tapped, and Full-Wave Bridge Rectifier. Derive DC Output Voltage ($V_{dc} = \frac{2 V_m}{\pi}$), RMS current, Ripple Factor ($\gamma = 0.482$), Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV), and Rectification Efficiency ($\eta = 81.2\%$) with capacitive filter.

In a bridge rectifier circuit, the input AC voltage is $230\text{ V}, 50\text{ Hz}$ through a step-down transformer of turns ratio $10:1$. If the load resistance is $1000\;\Omega$, calculate: (a) DC output voltage, (b) DC load current, (c) Ripple voltage with $100\;\mu\text{F}$ filter capacitor, (d) PIV of each diode.

Explain Zener Diode Voltage Regulator circuit. Calculate the series limiting resistance $R_s$ and maximum Zener current $I_{Z\max}$ for a regulator maintaining $10\text{ V}$ across a load of $500\;\Omega$ with input voltage varying from $15\text{ V}$ to $22\text{ V}$.

Explain Bipolar Junction Transistor (BJT): NPN and PNP configurations (CB, CE, CC). Explain Common Emitter (CE) Input and Output characteristics, Active / Cutoff / Saturation regions, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ relation ($\beta = \frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}$), and DC Load Line with Q-Point determination.

Explain BJT Voltage Divider Bias (Self Bias) circuit. In a voltage divider circuit, $V_{CC} = 15\text{ V}, R_1 = 33\text{ k}\Omega, R_2 = 10\text{ k}\Omega, R_C = 2\text{ k}\Omega, R_E = 1\text{ k}\Omega$, and $\beta = 100$. Calculate Q-point coordinates ($I_{CQ}, V_{CEQ}$).

Explain Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amp): Ideal characteristics ($R_{in}=\infty, R_{out}=0, A_v=\infty, CMRR=\infty$, Virtual Ground concept). Derive closed-loop gain for:
(a) Inverting Amplifier ($A_v = -R_f/R_1$),
(b) Non-Inverting Amplifier ($A_v = 1 + R_f/R_1$),
(c) Voltage Follower (Buffer),
(d) Summing Amplifier (Adder),
(e) Difference / Differential Amplifier.

Design an inverting summing amplifier using an ideal Op-Amp to produce output voltage $v_o = -(2 v_1 + 3 v_2 + 0.5 v_3)$ using feedback resistor $R_f = 60\text{ k}\Omega$. Find input resistors $R_1, R_2, R_3$.
Explain Op-Amp Integrator and Differentiator circuits with input and output waveforms. Derive output voltage expressions: $v_o(t) = -\frac{1}{RC}\int v_i(t) dt$ and $v_o(t) = -RC \frac{dv_i}{dt}$.
Explain Op-Amp Comparator and Schmitt Trigger circuit with hysteresis loop ($V_{UTP}, V_{LTP}$). State applications in waveform generation.
